title: Average query cost under the hard-input distribution
statement: Let $T$ be a finite decision tree that queries three sign-valued coordinates and returns a sign. Choose a seed uniformly from pairs $(s,r)$ with $s\in\{-1,1\}$ and $r\in\{0,1,2\}$, and form the input whose $r$th coordinate is $-s$ and whose other two coordinates are $s$. The average query cost of $T$ under the resulting input distribution equals the expected number of queries made by $T$ on this seeded input.
hypotheses_covered: The tree has three sign-valued input coordinates
